Key Technical Concepts:\n\n   **Pipeline**\n   - Steps: parse → understandingRules → inferTypes → meaningRules → contextRules → emit.\n   - The parser returns `node('SourceProgram', {language, items})`.\n   - collectItems (rules.js) handles the items:\n     - Comment and Blank items are pending trivia. Comments before the last Blank above the first code become file comments.\n     - Import gives `{text}` in program.imports.\n     - Function gives functions, with `comments` from pending trivia; `blankAfter` is set by whether a Blank came before the next item.\n     - Anything else goes to main statements.\n     - An item of kind `Statements` is spread (an empty one drops a form).\n   - recognizeCommonLibrary matches callees by `nameWords(callee).join('-')`, so `print-line` works. It filters imports matching `/common[-_]?library/i`.\n   - partsToValue(parts) (exported from rules.js) merges texts and drops empty texts. It gives Text '' for none and the single part for one.\n   - `add(left, right)` from meta/tree.js folds numbers. An inclusive end is `add(last, number(1))`.\n   - numberLiteral(written) gives a real when the text has `.`/`e`.\n   - The default lineCalls include 'print' and 'println'. The Lisp readers produce Print nodes directly.\n\n   **Meta nodes**\n   - Function {name, parameters[{name,type}], returnType, body}\n   - Declaration {name,type,value,mutable}\n   - Assignment {name, operator:'=', value}\n   - IndexAssignment {name,index,value}\n   - If {condition, then, otherwise}\n   - While {condition, body}\n   - CountingLoop {variable,start,end(exclusive),body}\n   - ForEach {variable,array,body}\n   - Return {value?}, Print {value,newline}, Evaluate {expression}\n   - Comment {text, trailing?, block?}, Blank {lines}\n   - Number {value} (type real when written with `.`/`e`)\n   - Text, Boolean, Name, Interpolation {parts}, Binary, Unary (negate/not), Call {callee, arguments}\n   - ArrayLiteral {elements}, NewArray {length, fill}, Index {array: Name, index}, Length {array: Name}\n   - ToReal {operand}, emitted via `toReal`/castText\n   - Negative literals are Number(-5); `-x` is Unary negate.\n   - Expressions carry `.type` after inferTypes.\n\n   **Emitter (js/src/formal/emitter.js)**\n   - `Emitter = withReals(withArrays(BaseEmitter))`.\n   - BaseEmitter fields: syntax, id, unit, lines, depth, uses.\n   - `line()`.\n   - `comment(text,{trailing,block})` uses commentLines; a single-line trailing comment is appended to the last line with its gap.\n   - `blank(lines)`.\n   - `body(block)` runs layout() and then statement().\n   - `program()`: forwardDeclarations (laterCalls, `this.forwardDeclaration(item)`), functions (blank line after when `blankAfter !== false`), then main; pops trailing ''; prepends the file comments plus a blank line, then `prelude(program)` (syntax.prelude plus program.libraryImports plus a blank line).\n   - The prelude is computed after the body, so a \"uses reals\" flag set during the body works.\n   - `expression()` base cases; Boolean uses syntax.words.\n   - `escape()` handles `\\\\ \\\" \\n \\t \\r`.\n   - The dialect emitter is `dialects[id].emitter(Emitter)`; the parser is `dialects[id].parser(Parser)`.\n   - The BaseParser constructor reads syntax.operators {remainder, integerDivide, and, or, equal, notEqual}.\n\n   **Lexer (js/src/formal/lexer.js)**\n   - Exports SyntaxError, decodeEscapes, commentText, blockCommentText, tokenize.\n   - The Lexer class has readers, push(type,value,extra), pushComment (trailing gap), and a newline handler that counts blanks only at depth 0.\n   - Token fields: type, value, line, span, trailing, block, quote, style, decoded, blank.\n   - Name spans are used by translation/identifier-language.js (in-place renaming; conventionOf splits on `_` only).\n\n   **Fragments (translation/fragments.js)**\n   - Statements are written between the marker comments `universal-translator-fragment-start`/`-end` in main.\n   - Functions get a closing function `fragmentEnd`.\n   - The wrapper puts the source fragment in place of the marker comment line.\n   - Announcements (forward declarations) of later-called functions are kept.\n\n   **Vocabulary (vocabulary.js)**\n   - Every string or string-array syntax field, except the notWords, is a concept. notWords: id, label, version, custom, naming, blocks, entryPoint, typed, arrayFill, forEach, forwardDeclarations, functionForm, immutableParameters, terms, symbols, escapeSigils, quotes, declarations, printCalls, commandCalls, textConversions.\n   - vocabulary-effect.test.js checks that each concept changes the writing or the reading. Problem Solving (settled design):\n\n   **Form lexer: new module js/src/formal/form-lexer.js**\n   - lexer.js's tokenize dispatches to it when `syntax.blocks === 'forms'` (the module cycle is OK). It imports SyntaxError, commentText and blockCommentText.\n   - Newline tokens are made at every depth, with blank counts, and never at the very start.\n   - Comments:\n     - blockComment comes from syntax.blockComment (`#|`/`|#`), using blockCommentText, block:true and span.\n     - Any `;` drops the whole run of `;`, then applies commentText.\n     - syntax.lineComment is also honored when it does not start with `;` (vocabulary effect).\n     - Trailing comments are detected as in pushComment.\n   - Strings: `\"` strings may span lines and count lines. CL decodes `\\x`→x; Clojure uses decodeEscapes. Push 'text' with decoded:true.\n   - Symbols: ( ) [ ] { } ' @. Clojure treats `,` as whitespace.\n   - Atoms: `/^[^\\s()\\[\\]{}\"';,@`~^]+/u`.\n     - A number matches `/^[+-]?\\d+(\\.\\d+)?([eEdD][+-]?\\d+)?$/`; replace d/D with e.\n     - Otherwise it is a name with a span. CL earmuffs `*x*` (length > 2) give name x with the inner span.\n   - An unknown character raises SyntaxError \"Unexpected character\". Push newline at the end if needed, then 'end'.\n\n   **Form tree (dialects/sexpr.js, shared core)**\n   - Node shapes: list/vector {items, line}, quote, deref, name/number/text atoms, comment trivia (trailing), blank trivia (newline blank>0 after earlier items).\n   - Trailing comment after a run of closing parens: attach the comment object to every list closed in that run. The statement converter converts inner bodies first and emits the comment after the first (deepest) statement form whose attached comment is not yet used.\n   - Comments inside expressions are dropped.\n\n   **Lisp writer helper (sexpr mixin)**\n   - Two-space unit.\n   - `close(n)` appends the parens to the last line before any trailing comment. Track `codeEnds` (line index → code length) and a set of comment-only line indices. After a comment-only or blank last line, put the parens on a new line.\n   - Override comment() to record these.\n\n   **Common Lisp writing**\n   - Functions and declarations:\n     - `(defun name (params)` with body.\n     - The final Return (last statement, descending into let bodies) is a bare value. Other returns are `(return-from name v)` / `(return-from name)`.\n     - Top-level main Declarations are `(defparameter *x* v)`. Global names have earmuffs in main, and in functions unless the name is a function param or local. Override variable().\n     - Nested declarations are `(let ((x v))`; a run of 2 or more consecutive declarations is `(let* ((a 1) (b 2))`. It wraps the rest of the block (override body()).\n   - Control flow:\n     - If with no else is `(when c`; else/else-if is `(cond (c ...) (t ...))`.\n     - `(loop while c do`.\n     - CountingLoop: start 0 and end not add-1 gives `(dotimes (i n)`. Otherwise `(loop for i from a below b do`, or `to x` when end is Binary add(x, 1).\n     - ForEach is `(loop for x across a do`.\n   - Assignments: [REDACTED]\n   - Print: `(format t \"ctrl\" args)`.\n     - Text parts escape `~`→`~~`, `\"` and `\\`, and newline→`~%`. Non-text parts are `~a`; boolean parts are `(if x \"true\" \"false\")`.\n     - `~%` is appended when newline.\n     - Interpolation outside a print is `(format nil ...)`. A Text with a newline outside format is `(format nil \"...~%...\")`.\n   - Expressions:\n     - Booleans come from syntax.words (t/nil). Call is `(f a b)` / `(f)`.\n     - Unary: `(- x)` / `(not x)` (operators.not).\n     - Binary prefix forms flatten left-nested add/subtract/multiply/and/or.\n     - divide is `(truncate a b)` (operators.integerDivide); remainder is `(rem a b)`; realDivide is `(/ a b)`.\n     - equal: text uses `string=`, booleans `eq`, otherwise operators.equal `=`.\n     - notEqual: text uses `string/=`, booleans `(not (eq ..))`, otherwise `/=`.\n     - Arrays: `(vector 1 2 3)`, `(make-array n :initial-element v)`, `(aref a i)`, `(length a)`.\n     - Reals: realText literals; ToReal is `(float x 1d0)`. Prelude `(setf *read-default-float-format* 'double-float)` when reals are used; the reader drops it.\n   - lisp syntax entry: naming 'kebab', blocks 'forms', lineComment ';;', blockComment ['#|','|#'], quotes ['\"'], declarations [], operators {and:'and', or:'or', not:'not', equal:'=', notEqual:'/=', integerDivide:'truncate', remainder:'rem'}, words {true:'t', false:'nil'}, printCalls {line:[],text:[]} and textConversions [] if needed, entryPoint 'top-level', typed false, forEach true (if that is how for-each support is flagged; expandForEach checks `languageSyntax(target).forEach`), terms {call:'function call', routine:'function'}.\n   - Reserved: t, nil, pi, the emitted form names, and common CL names (list, count, first, second, rest, last, max, min, abs, mod, step, position, print, write, length, vector, format, loop, ...).\n\n   **Common Lisp reading**\n   - Top level:\n     - `defun` gives Function.\n     - defparameter/defvar give Declaration.\n     - `(load ...)` gives Import {text}.\n     - declare, declaim and the float-format setf are dropped.\n   - Body forms:\n     - let/let* give Declarations plus the flattened body.\n     - setf gives Assignment / IndexAssignment.\n     - when/unless/if/cond give an If chain (`t` clause is the else).\n     - `loop while`/`for from below|to`/`across` give While/CountingLoop/ForEach; dotimes gives CountingLoop.\n     - `(format t ...)` gives Print (newline if the control ends with `~%`; split `~a`/`~A`, `~%`, `~~`).\n     - return-from gives Return; progn is flattened.\n     - Otherwise the form is an Evaluate.\n   - Value functions are found by a fixpoint:\n     - a function is one if it contains `(return-from name value)`, or its tail form (descending through let) is a value form (atom other than nil, arithmetic/comparison/logic/aref/length/format nil/vector/make-array, or a call to a value function);\n     - its tail value becomes Return.\n   - `(if x \"true\" \"false\")` in format args gives x.\n   - kebab names work with neutralName (`move-disks` stays as is); `list_` reads back as list.\n\n   **Clojure writing**\n   - Functions and declarations:\n     - `(defn name [params]`; `(declare f)` for later calls (forwardDeclarations).\n     - Mutable variables are atoms: `(def x (atom v))` / `(let [x (atom v)]`, read with `@x`, assigned with `(reset! x v)`.\n     - Immutable variables are `(def x v)` / `(let [x v]`. immutableParameters: true.\n   - Control flow: `(when c`; `(cond c A ... :else B)`; `(while c ...)`; `(dotimes [i n]` or `(doseq [i (range a b)]`; ForEach is `(doseq [x a]`.\n   - Values: `(println x)`/`(print x)`; interpolation is `(str ...)`.\n   - Operators: `(= a b)`, `(not= a b)`, quot/rem, `(/ (double a) b)`.\n   - Arrays: long-array, aget, aset, alength.\n   - Syntax: lineComment ';;', no blockComment. operators {and, or, not, equal '=', notEqual 'not=', integerDivide 'quot', remainder 'rem'}. words true/false.\n   - CPS tail mode, for functions with non-final returns:\n     - A guard If is `(if c THEN REST)`; when the then falls through, REST is duplicated into it.\n     - A While with returns is `(loop [] (if c (do BODY (recur)) REST))`.\n     - A CountingLoop with returns is `(loop [i a] (if (< i b) (do BODY (recur (inc i))) REST))`.\n     - A declaration is a let around the rest; a bare return is `nil`; `do` holds several forms.\n   - Reader inverse:\n     - A tail `(if c A B)` whose A always returns gives If(c,A) followed by B; otherwise an If/else.\n     - The loop shapes give While/CountingLoop followed by R.\n     - cond gives an If chain.\n   - Example functions with early returns: ackermann, factorial, female, male, is_prime, move_disks (bare return), and primality's While/If/Return.\n\n6. Problem Solving: the COBOL encoding design (to implement).\n   - **Layout:**\n     - `*>` file comments, then a blank line.\n     - Main program: `IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.` / `PROGRAM-ID. MAIN-PROGRAM.` / `DATA DIVISION.` / `WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.` / 01 lines / `PROCEDURE DIVISION.` / indented statements / `STOP RUN.` / `END PROGRAM MAIN-PROGRAM.`\n     - Then each function program, with blank lines per spacedAfter so the tight test round-trips (blankAfter false must be expressible: no blank line between END PROGRAM and the next IDENTIFICATION).\n     - Comments go before IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.\n     - `PROGRAM-ID. F IS RECURSIVE.`, then LOCAL-STORAGE (locals plus temporaries), then LINKAGE (params plus F-RESULT unless a procedure), then `PROCEDURE DIVISION USING … .`, the body, and `END PROGRAM F.`\n     - Render the body into a separate buffer first to collect the temporaries it needs.\n   - **Function ending:**\n     - If the last statement is a Return, append '.' to its last line; otherwise add `GOBACK.`\n     - Reader: '.' is a separator (skipLines also skips '.'). It drops STOP RUN and the final GOBACK.\n     - MOVE/COMPUTE into F-RESULT followed by GOBACK → Return(v). A bare GOBACK → Return().\n   - **Hoisting temporaries:** expressions push lines before the statement.\n     - ARGUMENT-n and RETURNED-n: unique per body, typed.\n     - SHOWN-n (`PIC -(18)9`): renumbered per statement.\n     - SHOWN-REAL-n (COMP-2) for real prints.\n     - TRUTH-n (`PIC X(5)`) for printed booleans: `IF c MOVE \"true\" … ELSE MOVE \"false\" …`.\n     - Reader: stores pending values and substitutes them when it reads the name. Those statements return nothing, so filter falsy statements.\n     - The reader needs a types map from the 01 declarations (PIC 9 = boolean, COMP-2 = real, PIC X = text), including the RETURNED-n type, to read `RETURNED-1 = 1` as the call itself.\n   - **Calls:**\n     - Name arguments are passed directly; others go through ARGUMENT-n.\n     - A procedure call has no BY REFERENCE and reads as Evaluate(Call).\n     - With no parameters: `CALL \"F\" USING BY REFERENCE RETURNED-n`, or `CALL \"F\"`.\n     - Calls in while conditions throw. and/or evaluate calls eagerly (documented).\n   - **Prints:**\n     - DISPLAY parts in order: integers via SHOWN, text vars via `FUNCTION TRIM(X TRAILING)`, literals with doubled quotes, reals directly.\n     - No newline → `WITH NO ADVANCING`.\n     - The reader builds Print with joined(parts) (empty → text(''), one → part, else Interpolation type text).\n   - **Booleans:**\n     - Stored as `PIC 9` 1/0.\n     - A value assignment is [REDACTED]\n     - In conditions: a boolean name is `B = 1`; true/false are `1 = 1` and `1 = 0`; not is `NOT (…)`.\n     - Comparing booleans (`c != d`): operands are written as plain names. A condition-valued operand throws.\n   - **Reals:** COMP-2. Integer literals moved into COMP-2 targets read back as real.\n   - **Control flow:**\n     - If-chains: `EVALUATE TRUE / WHEN … / WHEN OTHER / END-EVALUATE`. If later conditions contain calls, use nested IF/ELSE; the reader collapses an ELSE holding a single If.\n     - A single if: `IF … ELSE … END-IF`.\n     - While: `PERFORM UNTIL NOT (cond) … END-PERFORM`.\n     - Counting loop: `PERFORM VARYING I FROM s BY 1 UNTIL I > last`; the reader sets end = add(last, number(1)).\n   - **Division:**\n     - Integer division assigned to a var: `DIVIDE A BY B GIVING X`.\n     - Otherwise `FUNCTION INTEGER-PART(a / b)`; remainder `FUNCTION REM(a, b)`; realDivide `/`.\n   - **Arrays:**\n     - Declared as `01 X-LENGTH PIC S9(18).` / `01 X-TABLE.` / `    05 X PIC S9(18) OCCURS 0 TO 100000 DEPENDING ON X-LENGTH.`\n     - NewArray: `MOVE n TO X-LENGTH` ↔ Assignment(X, NewArray(n, 0)); arrayFill 'always' gives a fill loop.\n     - ArrayLiteral is written on one line: `MOVE k TO X-LENGTH MOVE a TO X(1) …`.\n     - Length is `X-LENGTH` (the reader yields `Call('length',[Name X])` or Length).\n     - An element target `X(e)` → IndexAssignment(X, offset(e,-1)). Element reads are Calls → Index via recognizeArrays.\n     - Array parameters are unsupported.\n   - **Text:** `PIC X(255)`; interpolation through `FUNCTION CONCATENATE` with trimmed parts. Trailing spaces are lost (documented).\n   - **Fragments:** the declarations wrapper needs `01 fragmentVariable PIC S9(18).` plus `MOVE 0 TO fragmentVariable`. Statement fragments must parse without a PROGRAM wrapper only via the wrappers.\n   - **Documented limits:**\n     - functions cannot see main's variables\n     - collisions with temporaries and with -LENGTH/-TABLE/-RESULT names\n     - the -VALUE ambiguity\n     - the 31-character name length\n     - real display differences\n   - **languages.js entry (planned):**\n     - naming 'cobol', label 'COBOL', arrayBase 1, arrayFill 'always', blocks 'keywords', caseInsensitive true, lineComment '*>', quotes ['\"'], doubledQuotes true, declarations [], compoundAssignment false\n     - operators {and:'AND', or:'OR', not:'NOT', equal:'=', notEqual:'<>'}\n     - entryPoint 'top-level', typed 'annotation'\n     - types {integer:'PIC S9(18)', text:'PIC X(255)', boolean:'PIC 9', nothing:''}\n     - terms {call:'program call', routine:'program'}\n     - The Rust twin goes in more_languages.rs.\n\n6. []), ...comments],\n  });\n}\n\n// The classes of objects of a program collected by findEntryPoint, read\n// with their objects: `this.width`, `shape.area()` and `new Rectangle(3, 4)`\n// become Member, MethodCall and New.\nexport function raiseObjects(program, from) {\n  const raw = program.classes ?? Key Technical Concepts:\n   - **Pipeline:**\n     - parse → SourceProgram items, then the understanding rules in order: findEntryPoint, concatenationOperator, integerDivisionCalls, recognizeArrays, recognizeCommonLibrary, recognizePrint, dropTextConversions, dropEmptyStatements, expandCompoundAssignment, dropParameterCopies, declareOnFirstAssignment, raiseCountingLoops, raiseArrayFills, raiseForEach, raiseTruthValues, inferMutability, dropSourceDetails, neutralNames.\n     - findEntryPoint turns a Function named `main` into program.main and sets `mainComments`. Comments before a function become its comments; Blank items set blankAfter.\n     - neutralName = nameWords (splits camel and `_`) joined with `-`. So `Sum_1` would become `sum-1`; the parser must strip versions.\n     - spellNames gives functions snake case and variables Pascal case (from `{function:'snake', variable:'pascal'}`).\n     - avoidReserved appends `_` when the lowercase spelled name is reserved.\n     - Undeclared names stay as written, so the emitter must force a leading capital.\n   - **Equivalence** ignores blankAfter, comments, imports, mainComments, mutable, returnType, type, Blank/Comment, elementsAssigned and imprecision. Otherwise it is strictly structural.\n   - **Fragments:**\n     - Statements wrapper: main with a `% universal-translator-fragment` marker line, which the fragment replaces.\n     - Functions wrapper: the fragment goes above the marker comment over `fragment_end(Result) :- Result = 0.`.\n     - Declarations wrapper: only used if the marker variable appears on more than one line.\n     - The source is first parsed as a whole program. programKind gives 'program' if `mainComments !== undefined`, so a fragment without a `main` clause must not set it.\n     - Writing emits a program with `-start`/`-end` marker comments and takes the lines between them, dedented.\n   - **Lexer:**\n     - Skips syntax.header if the source startsWith it. syntax.symbols come before the defaults (which include `//`, `>>`, `->`, `==`, `>=`, `<=`).\n     - Newlines inside ( and [ are not tokens; newline tokens carry `blank`.\n     - Names match `[\\p{Alphabetic}_][\\p{Alphabetic}\\p{N}_]*`, so `_` and `_X` are names.\n     - Text is decoded with decodeEscapes. The number regex `\\d+(\\.\\d+)?([eE]...)?` means a clause-ending `1.` is safe.\n   - **BaseEmitter:**\n     - line, lines, depth, unit (4 spaces).\n     - comment(text,{trailing,block}): a trailing comment is appended to the last line.\n     - blank; expression(expr, parent) dispatches Number, Text, Boolean, Name→variable(), Interpolation, Call, Unary, Binary.\n     - binary: precedence or1 and2 eq3 cmp4 add5 mul6. Divide uses operators.integerDivide; other operators use syntax.operators[op] ?? symbols.\n     - escape() handles `\\\\ \" \\n \\t \\r`.\n     - program(): functions (a blank after each unless blankAfter===false), then main(program), then trailing blanks are popped; file comments + prelude + body. Rocq returns `${header}\\n${super.program(program)}`.\n     - The emitter is withReals(withArrays(BaseEmitter)). withReals only converts operands for languages in `casts`; prolog is not in casts.\n   - **Dialects:** registered in dialects/index.js as `{ parser: (Base)=>class, emitter: (Base)=>class }`. The parser's item() returns nodes; `node('Statements',{statements:[]})` skips an item.\n   - **Native:** /tmp/ut-native/bin/swipl runs files by absolute worktree path. Never load yall explicitly: the autoloaded `>>` gives copy semantics, so lambda variables unbound at call time are fresh per call.\n\n3. Files and Code Sections:\n   - **Created: js/src/formal/prolog-runtime.js** (current content):\n     ```js\n     // The runtime that opens every Prolog program: loops that thread a state\n     // through a lambda, and lists read and changed by position. The lexer skips\n     // it when it reads a program, and dialects/prolog.js explains how\n     // statements use it.\n     export const prologRuntime = [\n       ':- initialization(main, main).',\n       '',\n       'loop_while(Condition, Body, State, Final) :-',\n       '    (   call(Condition, State)',\n       '    ->  call(Body, State, Next),',\n       '        loop_while(Condition, Body, Next, Final)',\n       '    ;   Final = State',\n       '    ).',\n       '',\n       'for_range(Start, End, Body, State, Final) :-',\n       '    First is Start,',\n       '    Last is End,',\n       '    count_up(First, Last, Body, State, Final).',\n       '',\n       'count_up(Index, Last, Body, State, Final) :-',\n       '    (   Index < Last',\n       '    ->  call(Body, Index, State, Next),',\n       '        Following is Index + 1,',\n       '        count_up(Following, Last, Body, Next, Final)',\n       '    ;   Final = State',\n       '    ).',\n       '',\n       'list_item(Array, Index, Value) :-',\n       '    Position is Index,',\n       '    nth0(Position, Array, Value).',\n       '',\n       'list_with_item(Array, Index, Value, Result) :-',\n       '    Position is Index,',\n       '    length(Before, Position),',\n       '    append(Before, [_ | After], Array),',\n       '    append(Before, [Value | After], Result).',\n       '',\n       'list_filled(Length, Fill, Array) :-',\n       '    Count is Length,',\n       '    length(Array, Count),',\n       '    maplist(=(Fill), Array).',\n       '',\n     ].join('\\n');\n     ```\n   - **js/src/formal/languages.js:**\n     - The rocq entry (line 788) is the template: naming, label, header, blocks 'keywords', lineComment, blockComment, quotes, symbols, operators `{...braceOperators, ...}`, entryPoint 'main-function', typed, types, terms.\n     - gml is the last entry (ends near line 843); Problem Solving — the final Prolog design (to implement now):\n   - **Syntax entry `prolog`:**\n     - naming `{ function: 'snake', variable: 'pascal' }`; label 'Prolog'; header prologRuntime; blocks 'keywords'.\n     - lineComment `%`, blockComment `['/*','*/']`, quotes `['\"']`.\n     - symbols `[':-','=:=','=\\\\=','=<','\\\\+','\\\\==','->','>>','//']`.\n     - operators `{...braceOperators, and: ',', or: ';', not: '\\\\+', equal: '=:=', notEqual: '=\\\\=', integerDivide: '//', remainder: 'rem'}`.\n     - entryPoint 'main-function'; typed false; terms `{ call: 'predicate call', routine: 'predicate' }` (or similar); extension `.prolog`.\n     - Add a vocabulary-effect `unshown` entry for any concept that does not take effect.\n   - **Reserved words** (lowercase):\n     - system predicates: is rem mod div xor format write writeln print nl halt true fail false not call catch throw length atom number integer float string var nonvar compound callable is_list between succ plus tab read once ignore forall findall bagof setof assert asserta assertz retract abolish msort sort predsort keysort functor arg copy_term atom_length atom_codes atom_chars char_code number_codes sub_atom repeat apply string_concat atom_concat nb_getval b_getval nb_setval b_setval consult ensure_loaded module use_module dynamic discontiguous initialization op phrase\n     - list library: append member nth0 nth1 reverse last maplist sum_list max_list min_list numlist exclude include foldl delete subtract select\n     - runtime: main loop_while for_range count_up list_item list_with_item list_filled\n     - plus s, result, v\n   - **Variable versions:**\n     - Placeholders are `\\u0001Base:id:flag\\u0001`, with a per-clause post-pass:\n       - id 0 is the bare `Base`; other ids are renumbered `_1..` per base by first textual appearance.\n       - A singleton with the pattern flag becomes `_`; other singletons become `_Name`.\n     - Allocation:\n       - A Declaration gets id 0 if its base is unseen in the clause, else a fresh id.\n       - An Assignment gets a fresh id. A read gets the current version, or id 0.\n       - Parameters get id 0. A loop variable gets id 0 if unseen, else fresh.\n     - Temps `V_k` use a clause-wide counter. `Result` is literal.\n     - Every variable name is forced to Pascal case.\n   - **Goal layout:**\n     - A goal-end stack per sequence. At the end of a sequence, `,` is inserted at the recorded column (before any trailing comment) on every goal except the last.\n     - If comment lines follow the last goal, or there are no goals, `true` is appended.\n     - The clause ends with `.`; a blank line follows a clause unless blankAfter===false.\n   - **If** (SWI layout `(   C` / `->  ` / `;   ` / `)`):\n     - Branches are emitted at depth+1, then the first line's indentation is replaced by the prefix.\n     - An else-if chain stays flat; an else Block holding an if is a nested parenthesized goal.\n     - Joins: the assigned variables (as in rocq's assignedVariables) that are live afterwards get join variables allocated up front, and each non-returning branch ends with `J = current`.\n     - A missing else becomes `;   <joins>` or `true`.\n     - Liveness walks a frames stack of the remaining statements:\n       - A plain Assignment or Declaration of the variable whose value does not read it makes it dead.\n       - Any other mention makes it live.\n       - At the end of a loop-body frame, the variable is live if it is in the loop state.\n   - **Loops:**\n     - While: `loop_while([s(In)]>>(Cond),\\n    [s(In), s(Out)]>>(\\n        body\\n    ), s(Init), s(Final))`.\n     - Counting loop: `for_range(Start, End, [I, s(In), s(Out)]>>(\\n body\\n), s(Init), s(Final))`.\n     - Start and End are passed unevaluated (the runtime evaluates them); calls in them are hoisted.\n     - Out comes from a placeholder replaced after the body. Final carries the pattern flag.\n     - With no state, the state is the atom `s`.\n     - State = assignedVariables(body).\n   - **Expressions:**\n     - Arithmetic is `X is E`. A Name or Number uses `=`; Text is `X = \"...\"`; a boolean literal is `X = true`.\n     - A boolean expression is `( C -> X = true ; X = false )`.\n     - Interpolation as a value is `format(string(X), \"..~w..\", [Args])`.\n     - Calls are hoisted left to right as `f(Args, V_k)`; a compound arithmetic call argument gets `V_k is E` first.\n     - Index → `list_item(A, I, V)`; Length → `length(A, V)`.\n     - NewArray → `list_filled(N, Fill, X)` and IndexAssignment → `list_with_item(A, I, Val, A_1)`. In both, compound arithmetic values are evaluated first.\n     - Evaluate of a value function → `f(Args, _)`; a procedure call → `f(Args)`.\n   - **Returns:**\n     - Tail returns (the last statement, recursively through the branches of a final If) become `Result is E` / `Result = V` / `f(..., Result)` / the boolean form.\n     - Other returns become `throw(return(V))`; a bare return is always `throw(return)`.\n     - Such bodies are wrapped `catch((\\n...\\n), return(Result), true)` or `catch(..., return, true)`.\n   - **Conditions:**\n     - Single line, with each comparison's temps inline before it.\n     - and → `, `; or → `( A ; B )`; not → `\\+ G` or `\\+ ( G )`.\n     - Integers use `< > =< >= =:= =\\=`; text and boolean use `==` / `\\==`.\n     - A boolean name is `X == true`; a boolean call is `f(Args, true)`; literals are `true` / `fail`.\n   - **Prints:**\n     - `format(\"text ~w~n\", [Args])` with `~` → `~~`; a text-only print is `format(\"Hello~n\")`; newline:false drops `~n`.\n     - Arithmetic parts are hoisted to temps.\n   - **Clauses:**\n     - A function is `f(P..., Result) :-`; a procedure is `f(P...)`, or `f` with no parameters.\n     - main is always written (`main :-\\n    true.` when empty).\n     - The program is header + `\\n` + super.program.\n   - **Reader:**\n     - A Prolog term Pratt parser:\n       - priorities: `:-` 1200, `;` 1100, `->` 1050, `,` 1000, `\\+` 900 fy, comparisons/`=`/`is` 700, `+ -` 500, `* / // rem mod` 400, unary `-` 200, `>>` 200\n       - arguments are read at 999; lists `[...]`; parenthesized terms are marked\n       - comments and blank lines attach to the goals of a conjunction\n     - Pre-scan clause heads whose last argument is `Result` (these are functions). `:-` directives are skipped; `main` becomes Function main.\n     - Name conversion: strip `_N`, then a leading `_`. `^V_\\d+$` names are temps, which are inlined.\n     - A version-0 base not yet declared → Declaration; otherwise Assignment.\n     - Skipped goals: joins `X_j = X_k` of the same base, and `true`.\n     - Return: `throw(return(V))`, and `Result ...` goals.\n     - The catch wrapper is flattened.\n     - Value form: `( C -> X = true ; X = false )` with the same variable → Assignment or Declaration of a boolean expression.\n     - In conditions, `X == true` → Name and `f(.., true)` → Call.\n     - `=:=` and `==` → equal; `=\\=` and `\\==` → notEqual.\n     - format strings: `~w` marks an argument, `~n` a newline, `~~` a tilde.\n     - loop_while → While; for_range → CountingLoop.\n     - list_item → Index; length → Length; list_filled → NewArray; list_with_item → IndexAssignment.\n\n6. Key Technical Concepts:\n\n   **Meta tree (js/src/meta/tree.js)**\n   - Kinds: Program{comments, imports, functions, main}, Function{name, parameters[{name,type}], returnType, body, comments, blankAfter}, Block, Declaration{name,type,value,mutable}, Assignment{name,operator,value}, If{condition,then,otherwise}, While, CountingLoop{variable,start,end exclusive,body}, ForEach, Return{value}, Print{value,newline}, Evaluate{expression}, Comment{text,trailing?,block?}, Blank{lines}, Number, Text, Boolean, Name, Interpolation{parts}, Binary, Unary (negate/not), Call{callee,arguments}, ArrayLiteral, NewArray{length,fill}, Index{array,index}, Length{array}, IndexAssignment{name,index,value}, and ToReal (numbers).\n   - essence/meaningDifference compare strictly, except the ignored keys: type, returnType, comments, mainComments, imports, mutable, elementsAssigned, blankAfter, imprecision.\n   - So a tail if/else and a guard If plus rest are DIFFERENT meanings.\n   - Exports: node, block, layout, number, text, name, add (simplifies), subtract, rewrite, walk, laterCalls, essence, meaningDifference.\n\n   **Parser flow**\n   - BaseParser.program() calls items(), which calls item() per top-level item; the result is SourceProgram.\n   - The understanding rules then run, in order: findEntryPoint (a Function named main becomes main), concatenationOperator, integerDivisionCalls, recognizeArrays, recognizeCommonLibrary, recognizePrint, dropTextConversions, dropEmptyStatements, expandCompoundAssignment, dropParameterCopies, declareOnFirstAssignment, raiseCountingLoops, raiseArrayFills, raiseForEach, raiseTruthValues, inferMutability, dropSourceDetails, neutralNames.\n   - collectItems: comments above a function go to it; Problem Solving — the refined OCaml design (not yet implemented):\n\n   **Two-stage reader**\n   - Stage 1 parses OCaml into small ML terms:\n     - seq items: let (with or without ref), comment, blank\n     - if, while, for\n     - assign (`x := v`), setIndex (`a.(i) <- v`)\n     - raise\n     - expr, unit `()`\n     - try\n   - Stage 2 interprets the terms in context (tail 'value', tail 'unit', or not tail).\n\n   **Sequences**\n   - Items are separated by `;`; `let x = [ref] v in` continues the same sequence.\n   - A term without a following `;` ends the sequence.\n   - In closed sequences (begin/end, do/done), comments up to the closer are gathered.\n   - In a top-level function body, only a trailing same-line comment is absorbed after the last term.\n   - The writer puts `;` after every statement except the last code statement. A sequence that ends with a declaration or is empty gets `()`.\n\n   **Tail mode (guards)**\n   - Used when every Return sits in guard structure: prefix statements with no returns, then either a Return v, or a guard If (no otherwise, its then-branch tail-structured) followed by the tail-structured rest.\n   - Valued functions:\n     - A guard is `if c then A else <rest>`.\n     - The rest is `v` alone, an `else if …` chain, or `else begin … end`.\n     - Never write `else a; b`: `;` binds looser than if.\n     - The reader treats a tail if/else in a valued function as a guard.\n   - Procedures:\n     - Tail mode only when every guard's then-branch is exactly [Return], written `if c then () else …`.\n     - The reader treats a tail `if c then () else B` as a guard.\n\n   **Exception mode**\n   - Used otherwise: a valued function whose last statement is an if/else where both branches return, returns inside loops (primality), or procedure guards with statements.\n   - Valued form: `let exception Return of T in try … raise (Return v) …; v with Return value -> value`.\n   - Procedure form: `let exception Return in try … with Return -> ()`.\n\n   **Refs**\n   - Assigned variables (including undeclared ones in fragments, and parameter copies `let number = ref number in`) are written `let x = ref v in`, `x := v` and read as `!x`.\n   - Unassigned variables are a plain `let x = v in`.\n   - Arrays: `[| a; b |]`, `Array.make n fill`, `Array.length a`, `a.(i)`, `a.(i) <- v`; no ref.\n\n   **Printing**\n   - Text: `print_endline \"…\"`.\n   - Otherwise `Printf.printf \"fmt\\n\" args`: %d for integer or unknown type, %s, %b, %g, `%%`.\n   - Interpolation outside a print uses `Printf.sprintf`.\n   - The reader turns these into Print / Interpolation itself, with partsToValue.\n\n   **Functions**\n   - Signature `let [rec] f (x : int) (y : int) : int =`, with `rec` only when the function calls itself or is in a group.\n   - Groups use `and` for laterCalls, as Rocq does.\n   - No parameters is written `()`.\n   - Main is `let () =` and is read as a Function named 'main'; an empty main is written `let () = ()`.\n   - A value nobody reads is `ignore (f x)`; a procedure call is `f a b`.\n\n   **Loops**\n   - `for i = a to b do … done`, with the end written as `add(end, number(-1))` and read back as `add(e, number(1))`.\n   - `while … do … done`.\n\n   **If statements**\n   - A simple single-statement branch goes on one line; otherwise use `begin … end`.\n   - else-if chains.\n   - Any branch containing a declaration uses begin/end.\n\n   **Expression emitter**\n   - Own precedence: or 1, and 2, comparisons 3 (operands at 4), concatenation 4, `+ -` 5, `* / mod` 6, unary 7, application 8, `!` / indexing 9.\n   - Application arguments are atomic, at parent 8.\n   - Negative numbers are parenthesized as arguments.\n\n   **Shared ML expression parser (dialects/ml.js, and a Rust twin)**\n   - Precedence climbing with per-language tables.\n   - Applications, dotted names, `()`, tuples (for SML's `Int.quot (a, b)`).\n   - An application hook maps calls to meta nodes.\n\n   **SML**\n   - `fun` with curried typed parameters, and `and` for groups.\n   - `let val … in … end`; refs.\n   - `while … do (…)`, and a `for_range` header function.\n   - Arrays: Array.fromList / Array.array / Array.sub / Array.update / Array.length.\n   - Division: Int.quot / Int.rem.\n   - Early returns through exceptions with `handle`.\n   - The header holds show functions that map `~` to `-`; the lexer skips it through syntax.header.\n   - Common library: `use \"common_library.sml\"`.\n\n   **Haskell**\n   - A pure Action-monad header (output accumulated). It provides pure, stop, loopWhile, forRange, printLine, a Display class, item, withItem, filled and size.\n   - blocks 'indentation', do blocks, `main = run $ do`.\n   - Operators: quot/rem, `/=`, `++`.\n   - State tuples as in Rocq.\n   - Common library: CommonLibrary.hs.\n\n6. without(part, 'static') : part));\n  return items.flatMap((item) => {\n    if (!isObjectClass(item, from)) {\n      return [\n        item.kind === 'Class' ? { ...item, items: unmarked(item.items) } : item,\n      ];\n    }\n    const statics = item.items.filter(\n      (part) =>\n        part.kind === 'Function' &&\n        !isConstructor(part, item) &&\n        !isMethod(part, from)\n    );\n    return [\n      node('ObjectClass', {\n        name: item.name,\n        items: item.items.filter((part) => !statics.includes(part)),\n      }),\n      ...unmarked(statics),\n    ];\n  });\n}\n\n// ---- reading the expressions on objects ----\n\n// \"shape.width.value\" as Member nodes, or undefined when the first word is\n// not an object.\nfunction memberChain(words, scope) {\n  const [first, ...rest] = words;\n  let object;\n  if (first === scope.receiver) {\n    object = node('This');\n  } else if (scope.objects.has(first)) {\n    object = name(first);\n  } else {\n    return undefined;\n  }\n  return rest.reduce(\n    (inner, member) => node('Member', { object: inner, name: member }),\n    object\n  );\n}\n\nconst objectKinds = new Set(['This', 'Member', 'MethodCall', 'New']);\n\nfunction raiseCall(call, scope) {\n  const { callee } = call;\n  if (callee.startsWith('new ') && scope.classes.has(callee.slice(4))) {\n    return node('New', { class: callee.slice(4), arguments: call.arguments });\n  }\n  if (scope.from === 'python' && scope.classes.has(callee)) {\n    return node('New', { class: callee, arguments: call.arguments });\n  }\n  // A method of an object that is not a name: `new Point(1, 2).norm()`.\n  if (callee.startsWith('.')) {\n    const [receiver, ...values] = call.arguments;\n    const isObject =\n      objectKinds.has(receiver?.kind) ||\n      (receiver?.kind === 'Name' && scope.objects.has(receiver.name));\n    return isObject\n      ?
